desk.why: Implied is 1.29x the forecast realised vol and no event that has measurably moved NIFTY falls before expiry.

facts: NIFTY moved +10.3% over the last 7 sessions and +2.0% on the day, to 25,030.
Almost no gap (+2 pts): the +492-pt body was built during the session, which is stronger evidence than an overnight jump.
The day closed at its high (close - low 642, high - close 0).
India VIX 17.47 (+12.1%) - rising on an up day: traders are paying for protection, the rally is nervous.
ATM IV sits in its 93rd percentile of the past year: option premium is rich - selling it pays more, but moves are expected to be bigger.

base.why: History says moves like this usually carry on (it reached 25,500 in 53.2% of past cases vs 37.7% normally), so the plan sells puts at 24,500, under the writers' floor at 24,800 and sells no call below 25,700.
text: bull put spread: sell 24,500 PE, buy 24,300 PE (credit about 40 pts, Rs 2,627 per lot; max loss Rs 10,373)

scenarios.title: Drifts sideways between 24,800 and 25,500
watch: Two daily closes below 25,500 without a new high
Close - open (the body) small, either colour
scenarios.means: The move is pausing. Time decay is working for the seller.
scenarios.action: Hold. Add a bear call spread: sell 25,700 CE, buy 25,900 CE (credit about 23 pts, Rs 1,484 per lot; max loss Rs 11,516) to turn it into an iron condor.

scenarios.title: Reaches 25,500 and stalls
watch: High - close bigger than close - low (sellers took it back)
25,500 CE open interest still rising (call writers defending)
scenarios.means: Call writers are defending 25,500. A ceiling for now.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 2,084 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell an iron condor, sell 25,500 CE / buy 25,700 CE / sell 25,000 PE / buy 24,800 PE. Call writers are defending 25,500: sell calls at the wall and keep a put spread under the market, so both sides earn while it stalls.

scenarios.title: Breaks out above 25,500
watch: 25,500 CE open interest falling (writers buying back - short covering)
Close near the day's high again
scenarios.means: The ceiling gave way. Next magnets: 25,700 then 26,000.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 2,242 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell a spread, sell 25,500 PE / buy 25,300 PE. The old ceiling 25,500 becomes the floor: sell puts at it. No calls below 26,000. Or buy a spread: buy 25,600 CE / sell 26,000 CE. If it spikes past 25,700 in one session with VIX rising, take profit instead of chasing.
scenarios.odds: Reached 25,700 in 34.0% and 26,000 in 25.5% of past cases (normal 23.7% / 12.5%).

scenarios.title: Pulls back to 24,800
watch: Holds: daily close above 24,800 and 24,800 PE open interest still rising
Breaks: daily close below 24,800 and 24,800 PE open interest falling
scenarios.means: A test of the put writers' floor. Shakeouts are normal after strong runs.
scenarios.action: If it holds: keep today's position, or add sell 24,400 PE / buy 24,200 PE (weekly). If it breaks: close today's position and switch to sell 24,800 CE / buy 25,000 CE (weekly). Exact strikes for every expiry are in the position matrix.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 24,800 at some point in 48.9% of past cases (normal 51.2%).

rules: Take profit on any spread once 50% of its credit is earned; the rest is not worth the risk.
Close any spread once its loss reaches 1.5x the credit taken, whatever day that is. Holding into expiry is fine; size smaller on expiry day.
Act on daily closes, not intraday spikes. The OI checks use the next morning's bhavcopy.
Credits for rolls and add-ons are set by prices on the day you act; today's numbers are a guide only.
limits: None of the desk's positioning signals (PCR, max pain, OI flow, walls) has passed its own backtest for this horizon, so the history study is the main evidence.
